builder: Custom build by Florida Lifestyle Homes (listed by eXp Realty)
incentives: None advertised: the listing doesn't mention a rate buydown or closing-cost credit. With the price down $704,000 from its 2025 peak, eight cuts so far, and the last one in mid-August, ask for a credit to finish the outdoor kitchen.
ratingWhy: New builds that have sat are being cut widely, but the wider Charlotte County market is holding its prices.
writeup:
Punta Gorda's resale market isn't collapsing. Charlotte County's median sale price was $320,000 in September, up 7% from a year earlier. Homes took a median 69 days to sell, and there were about 4.9 months of inventory. In Punta Gorda itself, homes have been selling for about 91.6% of asking, and nearly half of buyers pay cash, so buyers have room to negotiate.

New construction is where the pressure shows. We track 252 new-construction homes in Punta Gorda that have been for sale 60+ days. Eight in ten have been cut, the typical cut from peak is 7%, about a quarter are down 10% or more, and 17 are down 20% or more. This one is an outlier: a custom 2024 home on Lake Timber Drive, first priced at $1,599,000 in February 2025 and now $895,000. That works out to about $339 a square foot for 2,640 sq ft. The listing calls it move-in ready but says the summer kitchen is only plumbed, not built. A 3- vs. 4-bedroom discrepancy in the listing is also worth checking.
bottom: For the resale market, no bottom to call: prices are still edging up. For this house, the steepest cuts came in 2025. The current listing has dropped only once, from $945,000 to $895,000 in August, so the seller may be close to their floor. Our city trend data is only two readings old, too thin to say whether new-build cuts are still deepening.
